hook: A monochrome still image captured by a U.S. military system in 2025, submitted by the FBI to AARO, showing two small dark elongated objects near the center of the frame in the bottom-right quadrant against a grainy background with a central crosshair overlay.
why_it_matters: This image represents one of the rare instances where FBI-submitted visual evidence of a UAP has been formally incorporated into the AARO disclosure process. The fact that the original imagery was redacted before submission — and that no accompanying mission report was provided — limits the analytical value of the report significantly. The operator's inability to positively identify the objects, combined with corrupted metadata (incorrect system timestamp), underscores the documentation challenges that complicate UAP assessment even in formal military reporting chains.

key_findings.finding: The image was altered with redactions prior to submission to AARO, meaning the disclosed version does not represent the unmodified original capture from the military system.
The operator of the military system was unable to positively identify the UAP depicted in the image.
Two small, dark, elongated objects are visible near the center of the frame, specifically in the bottom-right quadrant of the monochrome image.
The image timestamp is unreliable: the date displayed in the image is incorrect due to the system's date and time not having been properly configured.
No accompanying mission report was provided alongside the image submission, leaving the operational context — including altitude, speed, sensor mode, and observer platform — undocumented.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: AARO is the direct recipient of this FBI-submitted UAP image, placing it squarely within the post-2022 formal UAP reporting and resolution infrastructure.

The use of a U.S. military imaging system and the involvement of military sensor platforms echoes the long legacy of military-collected UAP imagery historically processed through Air Force channels at Wright-Patterson.
